label: The numbers
title: Sixteen years of filings: the stores, the losses and the debt
lede: Blockbuster’s revenue peaked at $6.05B in 2004. Its profits had peaked long before. The company reported a net loss in thirteen of the fourteen years from 1997 to 2010.

blocks.title: The rise and fall, in stores
blocks.subtitle: Company-operated and franchised stores worldwide at each year end.

points.title: 1999: the IPO
points.text: Viacom sells 31 million shares at $15. The chain has 7,153 stores and late fees are 15.5% of revenue.[^1][^2]

points.title: 2004: the peak
points.text: 9,094 stores. The same year brings the split from Viacom, $1.45B of new financing and the launch of Blockbuster Online.[^5][^6]

points.title: 2006: the retreat begins
points.text: The count falls by 682 in a year, to 8,360 (difference derived).[^6][^8]

points.title: 2010: Chapter 11
points.text: 5,335 stores at the first year end in bankruptcy, 41% below the peak (derived).[^10]

blocks.source: Year-end store counts from the selected financial data in Blockbuster’s 10-Ks: 1995–1999[^2], 2000[^3], 2001–2005[^6], 2006–2007[^8], 2008–2009[^9], 2010[^10]. The fiscal year ended in early January from 2007 onward.

The large losses of 2002–2004 are mostly non-cash: a $1,817.0M charge for a change in accounting principle in 2002, and impairments of goodwill and other long-lived assets of $1,304.9M in 2003 and $1,504.4M in 2004.[^6]
